about: Expert questions, hand-written: how Pennsylvania towns regulate ADUs, the bills, site and size rules, confidence labels, how the tool works, places with no rule file, tricks, out-of-scope asks and follow-ups. Facts come from get_place_answer, get_rule_text and get_methods results.

questions.question: What is the difference between a special exception and a conditional use for an ADU in Pennsylvania?

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.rubric: Special exception: Zoning Hearing Board, at a hearing, under set standards. Conditional use: the governing body holds the hearing and decides.

questions.question: My township says a second home on my lot needs a use variance. What does that mean, and is it easy to get?

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.rubric: A use variance needs unnecessary hardship from the lot's unique conditions and is hard to get.

questions.question: How long does the Zoning Hearing Board have to hear and decide a special exception for an ADU?

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.rubric: First hearing within 60 days of a complete application, written decision within 45 days after the last hearing (MPC 908).

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.question: My lot in Canonsburg borough is in the floodplain next to a creek. How far back from the creek would a new building have to be?

questions.question: My Pittsburgh lot is on a steep hillside. Does that stop me from building an ADU?

questions.rubric: Steep slope rules are conditions, not a bar: grading rules (915.02) apply. Geotechnical report for steeper cuts.

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.rubric: Flood flag at 10 percent or more of the lot in the flood layer. Flags do not change the fit.

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

history.content: Can I build a detached backyard cottage in Plum borough, Allegheny County?

Plum borough, Allegheny County. Not allowed today except by variance for a detached backyard cottage (Table 12, 406). Source: Plum Borough Zoning Ordinance, 2026-11-13. Confidence: Checked rule file, verified on 2026-11-13.

questions.question: And how much parking does it need?

questions.rubric: Follow-up on Scranton: one off-street space per ADU (445-41W(1)).

history.content: Are ADUs allowed in Scranton city?

Scranton city, Lackawanna County. Allowed by right in most districts with a zoning permit (445-12, 445-38). Source: City of Scranton Zoning Ordinance, 2026-11-11. Confidence: Checked rule file, verified on 2026-11-11.

questions.question: Has it passed yet?

forbidden.pattern: \bI don'?t know\b|\bI do not know\b|\bI'?m not sure\b|\bI am not sure\b

questions.rubric: Follow-up on HB 2186: passed the House 139-62 on June 1, 2026, waiting in the Senate. Not law.

history.content: What would HB 2186 do for ADUs?

HB 2186 would allow one ADU per residential lot by right in every town with zoning, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh included. Towns could still set reasonable size, height and setback limits. It is a bill, not law.
